title: Protocol for Identification and Removal of Doublets with DoubletDecon

steps.title: Install DoubletDecon package
steps.instruction: Install the required R packages, download DoubletDecon from GitHub, and launch its Shiny user interface.

substeps.instruction: If the devtools package is not already installed, run: `if(!require(devtools)){ install.packages("devtools") }`
Install DoubletDecon from GitHub with: `devtools::install_github('EDePasquale/DoubletDecon')`
Start the DoubletDecon UI by executing: `shiny::runGist('a81cdc2aea5742c08e5fc3fa66d47698', launch.browser=TRUE)`

steps.title: Prepare input files for DoubletDecon
steps.instruction: Create the required ICGS‑style files either directly from ICGS output or by converting a Seurat object, then define the main DoubletDecon parameters.

substeps.instruction:
ICGS Variant: locate the three required files (no reformatting needed):
  i. Marker gene expression file: `~/Project_Name/ICGS-NMF/MarkerFinder/FinalMarkerHeatmap_all.txt`
  ii. Groups file: `~/Project_Name/ICGS-NMF/MarkerFinder/FinalGroups.txt`
  iii. (Optional) Full expression file: `~/Project_Name/ExpressionInput/exp.Project_Name.txt`

Seurat Variant: run the conversion function with the recommended defaults:
  `newFiles = Improved_Seurat_Pre_Process(seuratObject, num_genes = 50, write_files = FALSE)`
  - `seuratObject` must be a Seurat v3 object with cluster identities set to the original Seurat cluster numbers.
  - `num_genes` defaults to 50 (fewer reduces performance).
  - `write_files` should be set to TRUE for large datasets or when you plan to rerun DoubletDecon.
  The function returns:
    i. `newFiles$newExpressionFile` (ICGS‑style marker expression file)
    ii. `newFiles$newGroupsFile` (ICGS‑style groups file)
    iii. `newFiles$newFullExpressionFile` (optional full expression file)

Define the following DoubletDecon run parameters (replace example values as needed):
  - `filename`: a unique character string without spaces or special characters, e.g., `"AML_May5th_DoubletDecon"`.
  - `location`: full path to the folder that will contain both input and output files, ending with a trailing `/`, e.g., `"/Users/UserName/Documents/ProjectName/Doublets/"`.
  - `rawDataFile`: the marker gene expression file (`FinalMarkerHeatmap_all.txt` or `newFiles$newExpressionFile`).
  - `groupsFile`: the groups file (`FinalGroups.txt` or `newFiles$newGroupsFile`).
  - `fullDataFile`: the optional full expression file (`exp.Project_Name.txt` or `newFiles$newFullExpressionFile`).
Compare your generated files to the example files in the DoubletDecon GitHub repository (folder `Seurat_Conversion_Files`) to verify correct formatting.
NOTE: When using Seurat‑originated input, DoubletDecon will renumber cluster IDs by adding 1 to match ICGS format.

steps.title: Determine cluster merging parameter (ρ′)
steps.instruction: Select an appropriate ρ′ value that merges transcriptionally similar clusters while preserving biologically distinct ones, using either the manual console method or the UI testing tool.

substeps.instruction:
Manual Variant:
  a. Run DoubletDecon with the default ρ′ (rhop = 1) using `Main_Doublet_Decon(...)`.
  b. When the console prints "Creating synthetic doublet profiles...", stop the run.
  c. Examine the automatically generated cluster‑by‑cluster heatmap; yellow blocks indicate clusters that would be merged at the current ρ′.
  d. Adjust `rhop` up or down by 0.1 and repeat steps a–c until the heatmap shows an acceptable pattern of merged clusters.
  e. Remember that merging clusters prevents detection of doublets between those merged clusters.

UI Variant:
  a. Launch the DoubletDecon UI and upload all required files.
  b. Click the “Test for rho‑prime values” button.
  c. Wait several minutes for processing; a new tab will appear showing heatmaps for a range of ρ′ values.
  d. Choose the ρ′ that yields the desired merging (record this value for later runs).
  e. CRITICAL: The choice of ρ′ strongly influences DoubletDecon results; ensure you understand the cell‑type identities of clusters before finalizing.

steps.title: Choose additional DoubletDecon parameters
steps.instruction: Set the remaining DoubletDecon options according to their defaults and the characteristics of your dataset.

substeps.instruction: `only50 = FALSE` (default). Set to TRUE to generate only 50%/50% synthetic doublets; FALSE adds 70%/30% and 30%/70% mixes, increasing sensitivity at a slight loss of specificity.
`PMF = TRUE` (default). Enables pseudo‑MarkerFinder rescue of clusters that show unique gene expression not explained by synthetic doublets.
`useFull = FALSE` (default). When TRUE, the rescue step examines the full gene list; if used, adjust `min_uniq` accordingly (see below).
`centroids = TRUE` (default). Use cluster centroids for deconvolution; set to FALSE (medoids) if a cluster contains >40% suspected doublets.
`num_doubs = 100` (default). Number of synthetic doublets per cluster pair; increase for very large datasets (aim for ~10% of total cells).
`removeCC = FALSE` (default). Set to TRUE to remove cell‑cycle‑enriched clusters (requires internet and correct `species` code).
`nCores = -1` (default). Automatic core detection; set to a positive integer when running on a compute cluster.
`min_uniq = 4` (default). Minimum uniquely expressed genes per potential doublet cluster for rescue. Increase to 30 when `useFull = TRUE`.
`species = "hsa"` (default). Three‑letter code for species; only needed if `removeCC = TRUE`.
`write = TRUE` (default). Allows all text‑based output files to be written. Use FALSE only for testing many parameter combinations.
`heatmap = TRUE` (default). Generates expression heatmaps for original data, final non‑doublets, and final doublets; set to FALSE for very large datasets during testing.
CRITICAL: DoubletDecon overwrites files with the same `filename`; always choose a unique `filename` for each run.

steps.title: Execute DoubletDecon analysis
steps.instruction: Run DoubletDecon with the selected parameters either from the R console or via the graphical user interface.

substeps.instruction:
Console Variant:
  a. Load the package: `library(DoubletDecon)`.
  b. Set the working directory to the folder containing DoubletDecon code (needed for cell‑cycle gene files): `setwd("/path/to/DoubletDecon_folder")`.
  c. Run the main function with all parameters, for example:
```
results_DD = Main_Doublet_Decon(
  rawDataFile = paste0(location, "rawData.txt"),
  groupsFile   = paste0(location, "groups.txt"),
  filename     = "test_file",
  location     = location,
  fullDataFile = NULL,
  removeCC     = FALSE,
  species      = "hsa",
  rhop         = 1,
  write        = TRUE,
  PMF          = TRUE,
  useFull      = FALSE,
  heatmap      = FALSE,
  centroids    = TRUE,
  num_doubs    = 100,
  only50       = FALSE,
  min_uniq     = 4,
  nCores       = -1
)
```
  d. If using Seurat‑converted files, replace the first three arguments with the objects returned by `Improved_Seurat_Pre_Process()`:
```
results_DD = Main_Doublet_Decon(
  rawDataFile = Files$newExpressionFile,
  groupsFile   = Files$newGroupsFile,
  filename     = "test_file",
  location     = location,
  fullDataFile = Files$newFullExpressionFile,
  ...
)
```

User‑Interface Variant:
  a. Start the DoubletDecon UI (as in Step 1).
  b. Enter a project name (used as `filename`) and select the `location` folder.
  c. Upload either ICGS files or Seurat‑converted files.
  d. Set the ρ′ value determined in Step 3 and adjust any additional parameters from Step 4 (some fields appear only when relevant, e.g., full expression file when `useFull = TRUE`).
  e. Click “Run DoubletDecon”. The UI will automatically generate UMAPs and bar charts.
  f. To run a second analysis, close and restart both the DoubletDecon application window and R/RStudio before launching the UI again.
Pause point: after a successful run, you may wish to evaluate the generated heatmaps and output files before proceeding to optional steps.

steps.title: Optional: Run DoubletDecon multiple times
steps.instruction: Repeat the analysis several times to obtain a consensus set of high‑confidence doublets.

substeps.instruction: Run DoubletDecon once (using either console or UI) and evaluate the results as described in the Expected Outcomes section.
Save the list of predicted doublets (the row names of the `Final_doublets_groups` output) to a text file or an R object.
Repeat the entire run (steps 5‑6) the desired number of times (recommended 20), each time saving the predicted doublet list.

Load all saved lists into R and compute their intersection:
```
common_doublets = Reduce(intersect, list_of_doublet_vectors)
```
  The intersected set represents high‑confidence doublets.

steps.title: Optional: Compare with other doublet methods
steps.instruction: Combine DoubletDecon predictions with those from additional doublet detection algorithms using either intersection or union strategies.

substeps.instruction: Run DoubletDecon and store its predicted doublets (as in the previous optional step).
Run one or more alternative doublet detection tools according to their published instructions and store each set of predicted doublets.

Intersection approach:
  - In Excel, paste each list into separate columns and use the Venny web tool (https://bioinfogp.cnb.csic.es/tools/venny/) to generate a Venn diagram; the central region gives the intersected cell names.
  - In R, load each list as a vector and compute the intersection with `Reduce(intersect, list_of_vectors)`.
Union approach:
  - In Excel, simply concatenate all lists to obtain the union.
  - In R, use `Reduce(union, list_of_vectors)`.
NOTE: Ensure that cell identifiers have consistent formatting (e.g., no altered characters such as “.”, “_”, “-”, “/”) across all prediction files before merging.
